Title: Detecting Apples in the Wild: Potential for Harvest Quantity Estimation
Authors: A. Janowski, R. Kazmierczak, Cezary Kowalczyk, J. Szulwic
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Smartphones were considered a mass-accessible orchard capture device, but the paper focuses more on counting models and GNSS geo-positioning than on an explicit capture app or stabilization rig.
Metric Reported: Method comparison; YOLO recommended for the proposed solution
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Detecting Apples in the Wild: Potential for Harvest Quantity Estimation | 2021 | Apple orchards | Smartphones with camera + GNSS
Parameters Or Configuration: Smartphones with required image-acquisition accuracy; dataset of 1102 apple images and 3800 background images
Tool/app/algorithm/method: YOLO; Viola–Jones; Hough transformation; smartphone camera + GNSS
Summary: This pilot orchard study tested smartphone-based fruit counting for apples and recommended YOLO over Viola–Jones and Hough-based counting for a practical yield-estimation workflow. It is one of the clearest examples in the search set of smartphones being treated as the capture device for field orchard CV, paired with GNSS positioning rather than a specialized camera rig.

Title: EscaYard: Precision viticulture multimodal dataset of vineyards affected by Esca disease consisting of geotagged smartphone images, phytosanitary status, UAV 3D point clouds and Orthomosaics
Authors: Sergio Vélez, M. Ariza-Sentís, J. Valente
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: The paper explicitly documents a practical smartphone-and-GNSS capture workflow for orchard/vineyard field data, but gives no detailed app, codec, or stabilization protocol in the abstract.
Metric Reported: Dataset utility for disease detection and yield estimation; no capture-performance metric reported in the abstract
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: EscaYard | 2024 | Vineyards / grapevines | iPhone X; Xiaomi Poco X3 Pro; DJI Matrice 210 V2 RTK; Micasense Altum; RTK GNSS
Parameters Or Configuration: High-resolution images of individual plants; geotagged data; RTK GNSS location information
Tool/app/algorithm/method: Geotagged smartphone image capture; RTK GNSS logging
Summary: EscaYard is a precision-viticulture dataset built from geotagged smartphone images plus UAV data. The smartphone side is straightforward but useful: iPhone X and Xiaomi Poco X3 Pro were used for high-resolution vine imagery, and RTK GNSS was used to geotag the samples.

Title: Preliminary Results for Halyomorpha halys Monitoring Relying on a Custom Dataset
Authors: Francesco Betti Sorbelli, Lorenzo Palazzetti, C. Pinotti
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Relevant as a field-capture example, but the abstract does not specify the smartphone app, stabilization, synchronization, or preprocessing tools.
Metric Reported: Promising detection results; no capture metric reported in abstract
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Preliminary Results for Halyomorpha halys Monitoring Relying on a Custom Dataset | 2023 | Orchard pest scouting | Drone RGB camera; smartphones
Parameters Or Configuration: Suboptimal drone imagery noted; smartphones used as additional field capture devices
Summary: This orchard monitoring case study used both a drone RGB camera and smartphones to gather images for Halyomorpha halys detection. The abstract emphasizes the pipeline of decisions needed for automation, but does not name a specific phone app or sensor stack.

Title: Phenotyping of individual apple tree in modern orchard with novel smartphone-based heterogeneous binocular vision and YOLOv5s
Authors: Guanao Zhao, R. Yang, Xudong Jing, Haosen Zhang, Zhenchao Wu, Xiaoming Sun, Hanhui Jiang, Rui Li, Xiaofeng Wei, S. Fountas, Huijun Zhang, Longsheng Fu
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: This is one of the strongest explicit smartphone capture-method papers in the search set because it links the capture hardware to calibration and downstream phenotyping.
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Phenotyping of individual apple tree in modern orchard with novel smartphone-based heterogeneous binocular vision and YOLOv5s | 2023 | Apple orchards | Multi-camera smartphone
Parameters Or Configuration: Paired smartphone cameras; model simplified for deployment on smartphone
Tool/app/algorithm/method: Virtual focal method; YOLOv5s; pinhole camera model; standard binocular vision
Summary: A smartphone-based heterogeneous binocular vision method was developed for low-cost apple phenotyping. The paper explicitly says it used a pair of cameras on a multi-camera smartphone, then a virtual-focal method to create standard binocular images before YOLOv5s deployment.

Title: Toward Estimating the Crop Coefficient of Vineyards Using a Smartphone Camera
Authors: Jonathan Jaramillo, Justine Vanden Heuvel, Kirstin H. Petersen
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: The abstract supports a simple but usable ground-video protocol for vineyard imaging, not a specialized camera app or sensor-logging setup.
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Toward Estimating the Crop Coefficient of Vineyards Using a Smartphone Camera | 2025 | Vineyards | Smartphone camera
Parameters Or Configuration: Videos of ground under vine rows on a sunny day with resident vegetation
Tool/app/algorithm/method: Segmentation model; structure-from-motion; Paso Panel comparison
Summary: This vineyard study used a smartphone camera to record videos of the ground under vine rows and then estimated shaded area with a segmentation model plus structure-from-motion. The capture protocol is plain but explicit: smartphone video on a sunny day, with comparison against Paso Panel measurements.

Title: Framework for smartphone-based grape detection and vineyard management using UAV-trained AI
Authors: Sergio Vélez, M. Ariza-Sentís, Mario Triviño, Antonio Carlos Cob-Parro, Miquel Mila, J. Valente
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: The abstract is about on-device detection rather than capture protocol, but it does document a concrete Android field workflow.
Metric Reported: TDR 90.8% (MobileNetV2) and 89.7% (quantized MobileNetV2); 103 ms per image for quantized MobileNetV2
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Real-time kiwifruit detection in orchard using deep learning on Android™ smartphones for yield estimation | 2020 | Kiwi orchards | HUAWEI P20 smartphone; Android app
Parameters Or Configuration: 100 selected field images at 3968×2976 pixels; 8-bit quantization
Summary: This smartphone app paper for kiwi detection is useful as an example of on-device field capture and inference. It reports an Android app, KiwiDetector, using SSD with MobileNetV2 or InceptionV3 on a Huawei P20, with 8-bit quantization to speed inference.

Title: Real-time kiwifruit detection in orchard using deep learning on Android™ smartphones for yield estimation
Authors: Zhongxian Zhou, Zhenzhen Song, Longsheng Fu, Fangfang Gao, Rui Li, Yongjie Cui
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: This is a software-pipeline example more than a field-capture protocol; the abstract does not specify stabilization or logging.
Metric Reported: 99% accuracy on custom dataset with ResNet50
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Fruits Classification and Detection Application Using Deep Learning | 2022 | Fruits in general | Android smartphone
Parameters Or Configuration: Android device camera in real time; images sent to web backend
Tool/app/algorithm/method: YOLOv3; ResNet50; VGG16; Flask web framework; OpenCV/C++ pipeline
Summary: The abstract describes an Android app for fruit classification and detection that sends smartphone-captured images to a web backend for analysis. It does not focus on orchard capture mechanics, but it does document a real-time mobile/web data pipeline.

Title: High-Throughput Image Analysis Framework for Fruit Detection, Localization and Measurement from Video Streams
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Strong on downstream processing of captured video; the capture device/app details are not the focus of the abstract.
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: High-Throughput Image Analysis Framework for Fruit Detection, Localization and Measurement from Video Streams | 2019 | Fruits / greenhouse row scans | Video-stream vision system
Parameters Or Configuration: Video streams scanned row by row in a greenhouse
Tool/app/algorithm/method: YOLOv2; tracking; optical flow; projective transformation; denoising; voting
Summary: This video-stream framework uses YOLOv2 plus tracking, with online and offline variants that incorporate optical flow, projective transformation, denoising, and voting to improve fruit phenotyping from video. It is one of the clearer pipeline papers for processing orchard video after capture.

Title: IC3INA 2023 Index
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Not agriculture-specific, but directly relevant if you want to synchronize phone video with inertial or GNSS logs in a field protocol.
Metric Reported: Positioning accuracy impact; no numeric field-capture metric in abstract
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Time-Synchronized GNSS/IMU Data Logging from Android Smartphone and its Influence on the Positioning Accuracy | 2021 | Not agriculture-specific | Android smartphone logger
Parameters Or Configuration: GNSS and IMU data not driven by a common clock; implementation inside Android logger
Summary: This paper is a review-oriented piece on IMU-based smartphone sensing rather than an agricultural capture study. It is still useful as a methodological reference because it documents an Android logger and explicit time-synchronization for GNSS/IMU processing.

Title: Correction of distortions in image analysis for improved phenotyping of tomato fruit
Authors: N. G. Rabelo, S. E. S. Faria, D. V. Matos, V. M. Maciel, J. R. Magalhães, V. Z. Anastácio, E. Rodrigues, Alcinei Místico Azevedo
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Directly relevant for smartphone intrinsic calibration and distortion correction before orchard CV inference.
Metric Reported: Practical calibration evaluation; no single detection metric

Parameters Or Configuration: Standard proposed for number and shooting angles of calibration photographs
Tool/app/algorithm/method: OpenCV function; photogrammetry method; single-image rectification
Summary: This is a calibration study for mobile-device cameras. It compares an OpenCV-based method with a photogrammetry method and proposes a practical standard for the number and shooting angles of calibration photos.

Title: High Throughput Image Analytics Using Hough Transformation for Wheat Phenotyping
Authors: James Y. Kim, Myung-Na Shin, Ji Hyun Lee, Weon-tai Jeon, Seung-Woo Cho
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: This is one of the best explicit examples of a smartphone-ground-image preprocessing pipeline, albeit for wheat rather than orchards.
Metric Reported: Successful transformation and consistent image-alignment results
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: High Throughput Image Analytics Using Hough Transformation for Wheat Phenotyping | 2022 | Wheat | Smartphone camera
Parameters Or Configuration: Six sets of raw images; oblique view transformed to nadir view
Tool/app/algorithm/method: Hough transformation; stitching software; deskewing; row alignment; overlap trimming; resizing
Summary: This wheat phenotyping study used smartphone-triggered ground images and then rectified oblique views into nadir views using Hough-transform-based row detection. It also developed open-source stitching software for deskewing, row alignment, overlap trimming, and resizing.

Title: Calibrando una cámara digital
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Useful as a practical calibration toolchain reference for smartphone field imaging.
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: Methodology and Tool Development for Mobile Device Cameras Calibration and Evaluation of the Results | 2023 | General mobile imaging | Mobile devices
Parameters Or Configuration: Developed software application; standard photo-number/angle guidance
Summary: This paper describes a calibration workflow for image sensors in mobile devices, implemented in a software application. It uses OpenCV and a photogrammetry method and then evaluates the result with single-image rectification.

Title: A real-time fisheye video correction method based on Android smart-phone GPU
Authors: Zhiyong Peng, Xiaopu Zhu, Jun Wu, Zujun Qin
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Not agriculture-specific, but directly relevant if your orchard rig uses wide-angle or fisheye smartphone optics.
Paper | Year | Crop | Device Used: A real-time fisheye video correction method based on Android smart-phone GPU | 2020 | General imaging | Android smartphone
Tool/app/algorithm/method: Fisheye calibration; contour constraint; Levenberg-Marquardt optimization; cubic-box-mapping method; GPU acceleration
Summary: This is a general fisheye correction paper, but it is still a useful smartphone toolchain reference because it reports real-time video correction on Android using a calibration plus GPU pipeline. The abstract gives a reprojection error and a 25 fps runtime.

Title: Automatic Calibration of Smartphone Cameras : A Framework for Efficient Optimization of Camera Parameters Used in Image Stabilization
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Potentially relevant to capture-setup tuning, but the abstract is too sparse to support any detailed extraction.

Tool/app/algorithm/method: Automatic calibration framework; image-stabilization parameter optimization
Summary: This smartphone calibration framework uses OpenCV and is framed as improving image stabilization parameter optimization. The abstract is thin, but it is explicitly about smartphone camera calibration rather than general computer vision.

Title: Oblique Trellised Apple Orchard Photogrammetry for Early Phenology Tracking of Individual Plants
Authors: Michael R. Chang, C. Gunning, Marco Camurri
Key Finding For Capture Methodology: Useful as a distortion-correction reference, but it is outside your preferred date range and not orchard-specific.

Tool/app/algorithm/method: Regression-based distortion correction; image correction factors
Summary: This study corrected image distortion from different camera angles using a regression-based correction factor, with smartphone-captured tomato images. It is a clear example of pre-processing for field/phenotyping image correction, although not a detection benchmark per se.
